'''Philipp Habegger''' (born 23 July 1978) is a Swiss<ref name="CV-2010"/> mathematician and a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Basel]] who works in [[Diophantine geometry]].

==Early life and education==
Habegger was born on 23 July 1978.<ref name="CV-2010"/> He received his Ph.D. under the supervision of [[David Masser]] at the [[University of Basel]] in 2007.<ref name="MG">{{MathGenealogy|id=113581}}</ref>

==Career==
From 2008 to 2010, Habegger was a ETH Fellow at [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name="CV-2010">{{cite web |url=http://user.math.uzh.ch/habegger/cv-eng.pdf |website=Philipp Habegger |title=Curriculum Vitae |date=November 2010 |accessdate=5 March 2021}}</ref> He moved to the [[University of Zurich]] for a lectureship position in 2010.<ref name="CV-2010"/> In 2013, he was a von Neumann Fellow at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]].<ref name="IAS">{{cite web |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/philipp-habegger |website=[[Institute for Advanced Study]] |title=Philipp Habegger |date=9 December 2019 |accessdate=5 March 2021}}</ref> As of 2021, Habegger is a professor of mathematics at the [[University of Basel]].<ref name="Basel-Math">{{cite web |url=https://dmi.unibas.ch/de/personen/philipp-habegger/ |website=[[University of Basel]] |title=Philipp Habegger |lang=de |accessdate=5 March 2021}}</ref>

==Research==
Habegger's research focuses on [[height function]]s and their applications to [[unlikely intersections]].<ref name="IAS"/>
